# 📊 NBFC Daily Watch — Saturday, November 21, 2026

Weekend edition for Saturday, 21 November 2026 (IST). Covers Friday 20 November's close to early Saturday. Stock and index figures are Friday 20 Nov closes; the NSE and BSE are closed today. IBJA does not publish rates on Saturdays, so the gold rows are the 20 Nov PM session; AGLOC has posted its block for Monday 23 Nov, which applies from that day.

## 🔴 URGENT / High Impact

### Gold's worst week since March, and the lower lending ceiling that applies from Monday
Gold has just had its worst week since March. Front-month Comex gold ended Friday at $3,512.30 an ounce, down $367.40, or 9.47%, for the week — in the Dow Jones Data Talk carried by Morningstar (20 Nov, 18:53 ET), the "largest one week net and percentage decline since the week ending March 20, 2026". The Comex December contract settled at $3,515.40, −4.62%, and December silver at $41.07, −7.41%, the steepest fall on the board (The Edge's official-settlement wrap); the front-month figure and the December settlement are different contracts.

Domestically, IBJA's 999 rate for the 20 Nov PM session was ₹1,23,893 per 10 g (₹12,389.3 a gram), ₹5,638 per 10 g (−4.35%) below the 19 Nov PM session; the 916 rate was ₹1,13,486 per 10 g (₹11,348.6 a gram). From Tuesday 17 Nov's PM session, the earliest row IBJA still shows, 999 is down ₹10,308 per 10 g (−7.68%) — three sessions of change (18, 19 and 20 Nov), not a full week. There is no 21 Nov rate: IBJA states it does not publish on central government holidays or on Saturdays and Sundays, so the 20 Nov PM session is the latest published benchmark.

AGLOC's next block applies from Monday 23 November: maximum permissible loan-to-value ₹9,646 a gram at 85% — ₹439 below the 20 Nov block — with ₹9,078 at 80% (−₹414) and ₹8,511 at 75% (−₹387), on a jewellery reference of ₹11,348, itself ₹517 lower and equal to IBJA's 20 Nov PM 916 rate rounded down. The ceiling is a rupee figure per gram, so a lower reference lowers what the same pledged gold supports: fresh loans against the same grams are smaller, and existing loans written close to a ceiling carry a thinner cushion.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the ceiling that applies from Monday is ₹439 a gram lower than Friday's, so each gram pledged at the 85% band supports a smaller maximum loan and existing loans near a ceiling carry a thinner cushion. The sources checked give no Muthoot Fincorp LTV or loan-book figure for 20 or 21 Nov.
Sources: [Morningstar: Dow Jones Data Talk, 20 Nov](https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202611206877/comex-gold-ends-the-week-947-lower-at-351230-data-talk) · [The Edge, 20 Nov settlements](https://edgeconsultancykw.com/commodities-wrap-20-november-2026/) · [IBJA](https://ibjarates.com/) · [AGLOC](https://www.agloc.org/)

### Muthoot Finance's sixth straight down session; on CNBC-TV18's reckoning, its worst week since April 2025
Muthoot Finance (a listed peer, and not Muthoot Fincorp) closed Friday at ₹2,550.50, −2.58%, a sixth consecutive down session on CNBC-TV18's count, and fell over the week from ₹2,840.00 on 13 Nov to ₹2,550.50, −₹289.50 (−10.19%). CNBC-TV18, writing at 13:26 IST on Friday — before the close — said the stock had fallen in seven of its last eight sessions, was "down nearly 11% this week", and was on course for its "worst weekly performance since April 2025, when it had fallen more than 14%".

IIFL Finance fell 5.04% to ₹611.95 (week −4.55%); Manappuram Finance slipped 0.83% to ₹280.50 (week −8.93%). Over the week, the rest of financials went the other way: Nifty Bank rose 5.90% to 64,635.20 and Nifty Financial Services 3.65% to 28,871.20, while Nifty NBFC fell 1.06% to 56,033.41. On Friday the Sensex rose 1.08% and Nifty Bank 2.49%. CreditAccess Grameen rose 1.14% after Thursday's 52-week-low close and still ended the week −10.96%.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the peer moves price the same collateral repricing the lead story describes; Muthoot Fincorp is not listed, and the sources checked give no Muthoot Fincorp-specific figure for the week.

### Motilal Oswal keeps Neutral on the gold financiers and expects elevated Stage 2
What does the fall do to the book? Motilal Oswal's answer, as reported by the Financial Express (20 Nov, 15:23 IST): the September-quarter results of Muthoot Finance, IIFL Finance, Bajaj Finance and Manappuram Finance show "a broad-based increase in stage 2 gold loan assets", attributed "predominantly" to customers adjusting to the revised repayment architecture, "particularly the introduction of monthly interest servicing".

The brokerage keeps a Neutral rating on the gold financiers under its coverage — mainly Muthoot Finance and Manappuram — citing rising competition, the need to adapt to regulation and gold-price volatility. It expects elevated Stage 2 "over the next couple of quarters, with some migration into stage 3", and describes a transition to "structurally lower profitability".

Every line above is the brokerage's view — not company guidance, and not a finding about any company's book.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the brokerage's read covers the listed peer set, not Muthoot Fincorp. The sources checked give no Muthoot Fincorp Stage 2 figure; the latest published number is Stage III at 1.07% in the 14 Nov Q2 filing, against 1.41% a year earlier.
Sources: [Financial Express, 20 Nov](https://www.financialexpress.com/market/muthoot-vs-manappuram-how-rbi-gold-rules-and-stage-2-loan-stress-weigh-on-margins-4389621/) · [BSE: Muthoot Fincorp Q2 FY27 filing, 14 Nov](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/1b013a70-8ca6-4aff-ae25-9ef12e008024.pdf)

### Pledged tonnage rises at the three large lenders while its value falls
Moneycontrol's 20 Nov report (10:15 IST) puts pledged tonnage up at all three large lenders in Q2 FY27: Muthoot Finance held 204 tonnes of gold as security, against 197 tonnes in Q1 FY27; Manappuram Finance 70 tonnes, against 67 in Q1 and 57 in Q2 FY26; and IIFL Finance 69.3 metric tonnes, against 64.3 MT in Q1. The sources checked give no comparable Muthoot Fincorp tonnage figure.

The mechanism, in the words of Pinaki Nath Banerjee, CEO-designate of the Federation of Gold Loan Companies: "When prices correct, borrowers may have to pledge a larger quantity of gold to raise the same amount of money. Therefore, the tonnage of gold pledged may increase even when prices have moderated."

The market-level numbers point the same way. CRIF High Mark's Q2 FY27 data, reported by CNBC-TV18 on 18 Nov, show originations rising 27.2% by value to ₹8.15 lakh crore on accounts falling 4.1% to 369.4 lakh, with NBFCs' share by value at 31.4%, up about 4 percentage points quarter on quarter, in a market estimated at ₹23.3 lakh crore, up more than 60% over the past year. More rupees against fewer accounts is growth from the collateral's price, not from more borrowers. Moneycontrol also reported, without citing a circular, that the RBI "started to monitor bullion portfolios of banks and NBFCs" as gold cooled from its January highs — a media report, not a rule change.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none stated in the sources checked, which give no Muthoot Fincorp pledged-tonnage, LTV or auction figure for November.

## 📈 Market & Stock Summary

### Friday's close and the week: nine-month-high indexes, with the gold lenders left out
Indian shares rose on Friday 20 Nov. The Sensex closed at 83,919.71 (+897.96, +1.08%) and the Nifty 50 at 25,800.60 (+286.30, +1.12%); over the week the Sensex rose 2.9% and the Nifty 2.6%, both closing at nine-month highs (BusinessLine live blog, updated 20 Nov 16:03 IST). Nifty Bank closed at 64,635.20 (+2.49% on the day, +5.90% for the week), Nifty Financial Services at 28,871.20 (+2.02%, +3.65% for the week). Nifty NBFC closed at 56,033.41, +0.32% on the day and −1.06% for the week.

FIIs were net buyers of ₹10,308.42 crore on 20 Nov and DIIs net sellers of ₹4,859.80 crore (NSE provisional). The rupee closed at ₹92.67 to the dollar, a seven-month high and its first close below ₹93 since April, up 62 paise from 93.29 (BusinessLine, updated 20 Nov 18:58 IST). Brent January 2027 settled at $92.57 a barrel (+0.64%) — official settlements carried by The Edge.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none stated in the sources checked. The flows and the rupee are market-wide facts; Muthoot Fincorp is unlisted and has no market price.

## 🏘️ Sector Deep Dive — Saturday: the week the collateral repriced

Saturday has no fixed sector rotation; this is one short weekend read on the week, not a sector study.

The collateral repriced: front-month Comex gold fell 9.47% for the week to $3,512.30, the largest weekly decline since the week ending 20 March 2026; IBJA's 999 rate ended Friday ₹10,308 per 10 g (−7.68%) below Tuesday 17 Nov's PM session, three sessions of change; AGLOC's 85% ceiling for Monday is ₹439 a gram below the 20 Nov block.

The market split the same week: Nifty Bank rose 5.90% and Nifty PSU Bank 6.72%, while Nifty NBFC fell 1.06% and the three large listed gold-loan names fell between 4.55% (IIFL Finance) and 10.19% (Muthoot Finance); the Sensex and Nifty closed the week at nine-month highs. The volumes rose as the value fell: pledged tonnage was up at all three large lenders in Q2 FY27, while CRIF High Mark's Q2 shows originations by value up 27.2% on accounts down 4.1% — more rupees against fewer accounts, growth from the collateral's price, not from more borrowers.

The money was not the constraint: FIIs bought ₹10,308.42 crore of Indian equities on Friday and about $4 billion over the week; the rupee closed the week at a seven-month high of ₹92.67. The week's constraint was the collateral, not liquidity.

Where the sources checked have no figure, this report says so: there is no Muthoot Fincorp LTV, auction or Stage 2 number for November in the day's sources. Its latest published figures are the 14 Nov Q2 filing — Stage III 1.07%, CRAR 19.38% — September-quarter figures, not a reading on November's repricing.

# 📋 NBFC Regulatory Daily Report
**Date:** Saturday, 21 November 2026 (IST)

Weekend edition for Saturday, 21 November 2026 (IST). Covers Friday 20 Nov evening to Saturday morning; the NSE and BSE are closed today.

---

## 🔔 New Regulatory Updates Today

No new RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument on 20 or 21 Nov changes a rule that applies to Muthoot Fincorp apart from the one below, which is a rule already made that takes effect today. A representation to RBI is not a rule change, and none appears in the sources checked. What was checked is set out below.

### SEBI Credit Risk-o-Meter comes into force today
SEBI circular HO/17/11/22(1)2026-DDHS-POD1/I/23092/2026, dated 7 October 2026, introduced the Credit Risk-o-Meter as a mandatory colour-coded disclosure for debt securities. Its paragraph 5 says the provisions "shall come into force after 45 days from the date of issuance" — that is today, 21 November 2026. From today the meter is a mandatory disclosure in offer documents, abridged prospectuses, private placement memoranda, issuer and online bond platform provider (OBPP) advertisements, and OBPP web and mobile platforms. The circular inserts a new Chapter II-C in the NCS Master Circular dated 15 October 2025 and a new clause 14 in Annexure-XXIB, the OBPP minimum disclosures. Its scope covers all listed and proposed-to-be-listed non-convertible securities, commercial papers, securitised debt instruments, security receipts and structured debt/MLDs, whether issued by public issue or private placement. The meter carries six colour-coded risk levels mapped from AAA to D (A1+ to D for short-term ratings), and where several credit rating agencies rate an issue, the lowest rating applies. OBPPs must update the meter within 24 hours of a rating-change intimation from NSDL or CDSL, with automated systems, no manual overrides and audit trails.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: Muthoot Fincorp's listed NCDs (Tranche I is listed on BSE) fall inside the circular's scope for any future offer document, private placement memorandum and advertisement from today. The circular is a rule now in force, not a representation, and it changes no term of an already-listed issue.
Sources: [SEBI circular, 7 Oct 2026](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/oct-2026/introduction-of-credit-risk-o-meter-as-an-additional-disclosure-mechanism-for-debt-securities_105081.html) · [circular PDF](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/oct-2026/1791436170839.pdf)

Net for the rulebook: no new RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument on 20 or 21 Nov changes a rule applying to Muthoot Fincorp, and the one live change is the Credit Risk-o-Meter taking effect today.
